parallel.requirements: Recognized std-only Rust 2021, argument parity through std::env::args, exact output formatting, /output/test15.rs, Cargo project structure, and black-box inference.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent owned implementation, integration, assembly, and final verification while delegating one child to probe additional inflection behavior from the executable.
parallel.implementation: Created Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/inflection module files, and test15.rs, then patched the implementation to handle empty string pluralization, abort behavior, and bytewise demodulize output.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent wrote and revised the delivered files in /output, produced /output/test15 and target/release/test15, and listed the final file tree.
parallel.verification: Ran cargo build, direct rustc build, many cmp-based comparisons against the C++ executable, non-ASCII checks, no-argument checks, and empty-string abort checks.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed 2 of 41 cases, but pair evidence does not expose the specific missed cases or a coordination mechanism causing them.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, CLI parity, exact byte-for-byte output, /output/test15.rs, Cargo project, and black-box restriction requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single actor owned probing, implementation, project assembly, direct executable creation, and verification without delegation or child handoffs.
serial.implementation: Created Cargo.toml, inflection/check.rs, inflection/transform.rs, inflection/mod.rs, and test15.rs with the observed simple inflection rules and abort behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial actor built a self-contained project under /output, produced /output/test15 and target/release/test15, and checked the final file set.
serial.verification: Ran behavior probes, cargo build, rustc, a loop comparing normal cases, and a separate empty-argument stdout/stderr/status comparison.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation also failed 2 of 41 cases, and the accessible evidence gives no per-test detail tying those misses to a distinct serial process defect.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run worked from the prompt requirements for std-only Rust, exact CLI/output parity, Cargo layout, root test15.rs, and black-box inference.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received and followed the same requirements and prompt hash.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference is visible; both attempts targeted the same specified output and project obligations.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent delegated probing to probe_inflection while retaining ownership of implementation, integration, build, and final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor performed probing, implementation, integration, build, and delivery itself with multi-agent disabled.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used one child for exploratory behavior discovery; serial did the same kind of discovery in the main thread.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child returned a structured black-box findings handoff with CLI, pluralize, camelize, underscore, boolean, demodulize, empty-arg, and bytewise non-ASCII observations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run accumulated the same type of interface facts locally before implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel handoff was not lossy or ignored; it added edge-case information that the parent checked and incorporated.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel first added a Cargo library layout under src/inflection and test15.rs, then patched inflector.rs and test15.rs after edge-case verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial added a flatter inflection module layout and test15.rs in one implementation patch.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The file layout differed, but both implemented the same behavioral surface and both still scored 39/41 officially.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited for the child result after one invalid too-short wait attempt, then received the result and announced verification of the returned edge cases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There was no child result lifecycle; the actor continued local probing and implementation directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel child result was retrieved and used, so no missing join or trapped verifier result occurred.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Only the parent wrote the delivered project files; the child was a probing actor and did not contribute file changes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The single actor wrote all delivered files and produced the final executables.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No write collision, overwrite, or shared-workspace provenance problem is visible in parallel compared with serial.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran Cargo and rustc builds, multiple cmp checks against the C++ executable, then explicit non-ASCII and empty-argument checks after consuming the child report.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran Cargo and rustc builds, broad sampled output comparisons, and an empty-argument stdout/stderr/status comparison.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both accepted based on sampled black-box parity; the official evaluator still found two failing cases in each.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished within budget after about 261 agent seconds, with one child and no timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished within budget after about 227 agent seconds, no child, and no timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more time and tokens due to delegation, but no budget exhaustion or unfinished required work from coordination is evidenced.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation records both modes as failed, each with 39 passed out of 41 evaluated testcases. The concrete process difference is that the parallel parent delegated probing and then consumed the child handoff, while the serial run discovered and implemented edge cases locally. Because both produced complete builds, both ran sampled parity checks, and both ended with the same official aggregate result, the pair supports no outcome-differential concurrency error.
parallel_contributors: Child probing supplied additional edge-case findings before final revision and verification.
Parent retained ownership of implementation and incorporated byte-level corrections after the child result.
serial_contributors: Single actor performed local black-box probing, implementation, build, and verification.
Serial verification also included empty-argument abort parity before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The projects used different module layouts.
The official 2/41 misses are not identified in accessible pair evidence and are not explained by a parallel coordination boundary.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; supported process contrast only

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly created and revised the Rust implementation files, so implementation ownership was present.
There were no separately implemented components needing cross-agent integration; the parent integrated its own files.
The parent assembled the Cargo project, root entry file, and executables before final response.
The parent owned the end-to-end path from probing through build, verification, and final delivery.
Implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; the parent probed and implemented while the child was active.
The parallel run did not complete all investigation before starting implementation; probing and implementation overlapped and did not leave implementation deadline-constrained.
The indispensable implementation path was handled by the parent and completed; auxiliary child probing did not starve the critical path.
Only one child was spawned and the run finished without timeout, so there is no collective fan-out budget exhaustion.
The child received a probing role, completed it, and returned usable findings; no overbroad child scope left required work unfinished.
The executed child produced the needed black-box behavior report; no omitted known requirement made its work unusable.
The child did not implement a component that had to interoperate with parent code, so no missing cross-agent interface contract materialized.
The child handoff retained the salient findings, including empty-argument and non-ASCII byte behavior, and the parent acted on them.
Although the child report was detailed, the parent consumed the needed parts and made a targeted patch, so it was not unusably bulky.
The child report described current black-box behavior and was used immediately; no superseded workspace or requirement state was consumed.
No incompatible child reports or contracts reached the parent; the single child report was consistent with parent follow-up probes.
The final acceptance was based on builds and multiple whole-program comparisons; the official failure alone does not reveal a parent-visible unresolved integration gap.
No replacement or retry child was launched; the parent revised existing code after receiving new findings rather than repeating from scratch.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The child completed and returned a final answer; there is no explicit stop, cancellation, or interruption of an active child.
The parent built and placed the deliverables before closure; no ready candidate was left unpromoted or unpackageable at the deadline.
After the child-informed patch, the parent rebuilt and reran checks, so changes were not merged only after final verification.
No child produced a delegated implementation to join; the child produced findings, and the parent incorporated them into its own implementation.
The child probe result returned to the parent before closure, so there was no trapped verifier or probe finding.
No required child failed, aborted, or was cancelled; the only child completed with a usable report.
The completed child result was explicitly acknowledged and drove further verification and code changes, so it was not ignored.
The parent's first wait call only hit a minimum-timeout validation error, then a valid wait completed and the parent inspected the result.
There were not competing parent and child implementation paths; the child only probed behavior while the parent wrote files.
No two live agents edited the same source or configuration file; only the parent performed file changes.
No non-entry source owned by one agent was replaced by another; parent revisions were to parent-owned files.
The delivered entrypoint and binaries were produced by the parent, with no concurrent child-owned deliverable overwritten.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion invalidated another agent's final tree work; only normal parent build outputs were present.
Shared workspace use did not create unstable state or provenance ambiguity because the child did not write implementation artifacts.
No generated child artifact, cache, fixture, or tool output was consumed as stable implementation input; only observations from the executable were used.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The invalid 1000 ms wait and later successful 10000 ms wait were reviewed as one harmless result-lifecycle episode and rejected rather than split into Blind Timeout Wait or Missing Verifier Return.
The shared /output workspace was reviewed as one write episode and rejected because only the parent wrote deliverables.
